topic_summary: Analysis of the personhood boundary in abortion law: the contested determination of when moral and legal status begins, which structures who counts as a rights-bearer versus who may be acted upon. This boundary determines victim sets, authority structures for adjudication, and the extractiveness of enforcement regimes.

key_entities: Pregnant person (rights-bearer in autonomy frameworks; potential rights-violator in fetal-rights frameworks)
State (enforcement authority; interpreter of personhood boundary)
Medical profession (gatekeepers; implementers of boundary determinations)
key_tensions: Fetal moral status vs maternal autonomy (zero-sum when personhood boundary places fetus inside victim set)
State authority to define personhood vs individual/community interpretive autonomy
Biological continuity (gradual development) vs legal necessity for bright-line rules
key_mechanisms: Criminal prohibition (state enforcement against pregnant person or provider)
Civil liability (tort framework for fetal harm)
Gestational limits (temporal boundaries operationalizing personhood determinations)
Exception regimes (health, rape, incest carve-outs revealing boundary instability)
key_absences: Non-Western personhood frameworks (e.g., ensoulment timing in Islamic jurisprudence, Buddhist gradual-consciousness models)
Disability rights perspective on selective termination and personhood criteria
Economic class dimension: who bears enforcement costs when personhood boundary criminalizes abortion

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood boundary: the determination of when moral and legal status begins, structuring who enters the victim set and who holds rights to bodily autonomy
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested across religious, philosophical, medical, and legal traditions; state claims adjudicative authority but lacks consensus grounding

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at conception (fertilization)
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law tradition, Catholic moral theology, evangelical Protestant frameworks grounding personhood in genetic uniqueness and potential
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at conception; abortion becomes homicide-equivalent; pregnant person's autonomy subordinated to fetal right to life; high state enforcement extractiveness targeting pregnant persons and providers

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at viability (capacity for independent survival outside womb)
readings.authority_grounding: Roe v. Wade framework (1973-2022), medical-technological threshold, balancing test between state interest and maternal autonomy
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at ~24 weeks (technology-dependent); pre-viability abortion protected; post-viability state may prohibit except for health; enforcement targets post-viability procedures; viability line shifts with medical technology (moving boundary)

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at birth (complete expulsion from maternal body)
readings.authority_grounding: Common law tradition, autonomy-maximalist frameworks, some secular philosophical positions grounding personhood in social existence rather than biological potential
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus never enters victim set; pregnant person sole rights-holder throughout gestation; abortion is medical procedure without homicide dimension; minimal state enforcement; no victim to protect pre-birth

readings.commitment: Moral status increases gradually across gestation; no single bright-line boundary but escalating state interest and moral weight
readings.authority_grounding: Philosophical gradualism (e.g., Warren, Tooley), some Buddhist frameworks, developmental neuroscience perspectives on consciousness emergence
readings.expected_structural_delta: No fixed victim-set entry point; proportionality framework where justification burden increases with gestational age; trimester-based or developmental-milestone regulatory schemes; enforcement intensity scales with fetal development; permits nuanced exceptions but creates legal uncertainty

axiom_contradictions.basis: Conception reading's axiom (genetic uniqueness confers full moral status) is mutually exclusive with birth reading's axiom (personhood requires social existence/independence from maternal body). No single coherent framework can hold both: accepting conception's axiom requires rejecting birth's axiom as false, and vice versa.

Conception reading's axiom (personhood is binary and present from fertilization) is mutually exclusive with gradualist reading's axiom (moral status is scalar and emerges across development). No framework can hold both: gradualism requires rejecting the binary-from-conception claim as false.

axes.structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at conception; abortion becomes homicide-equivalent
axes.primary_observable: Criminal abortion statutes with conception-based definitions; fetal homicide laws applying from fertilization; enforcement targeting pregnant persons
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct structural delta; highest extractiveness; generates complete victim set and enforcement regime

axes.human_readable: Viability Reading (Personhood at Independent Survival Capacity)
axes.structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at technology-dependent viability threshold (~24 weeks); pre-viability autonomy protected
axes.primary_observable: Gestational limits at viability; medical technology advancement shifting boundary; Roe/Casey framework implementation
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct structural delta; moving boundary dependent on medical technology; different victim-set entry point and enforcement structure than conception reading

axes.structural_delta: Fetus never enters victim set; pregnant person sole rights-holder throughout gestation
axes.primary_observable: Abortion-permissive statutes with no gestational limits; common law born-alive rule; absence of fetal homicide provisions
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct structural delta; eliminates victim set entirely; autonomy-maximalist framework with minimal enforcement

axes.human_readable: Gradualist Reading (Scalar Moral Status Across Development)
axes.structural_delta: No fixed victim-set entry; proportionality framework where justification burden increases with gestational age
axes.primary_observable: Trimester frameworks; developmental milestone regulations; sliding-scale justification requirements; exception regimes varying by gestational age
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct structural delta; rejects bright-line boundary in favor of scalar framework; generates different enforcement structure (proportionality rather than prohibition)

axes.structural_delta: The material and liberty costs imposed by state enforcement of personhood boundary determinations
axes.primary_observable: Incarceration rates for abortion-related offenses; forced pregnancy continuation rates; maternal mortality in prohibition regimes; cross-border travel costs; underground procedure risks
axes.selection_reason: Independent axis measuring enforcement costs; distinct observable (coercion intensity) separate from boundary location; downstream of conception reading but measures different structural dimension

axes.structural_delta: Physicians positioned as interpreters and enforcers of personhood boundary through exception regimes and mandatory procedures
axes.primary_observable: Mandatory ultrasound laws; waiting periods; provider criminal liability statutes; conscience clause invocations; exception certification requirements
axes.selection_reason: Independent axis measuring gatekeeping structure; distinct from boundary location (measures who interprets/enforces rather than where boundary is); affects extractiveness through procedural barriers

axes.structural_delta: Personhood boundary enforcement costs fall disproportionately on economically disadvantaged pregnant persons
axes.primary_observable: Cross-state travel costs; private vs public insurance coverage; income-stratified abortion access rates; wealth-correlated prosecution rates
axes.selection_reason: Independent axis measuring distributional dimension; distinct observable (wealth-stratified access) separate from boundary location or enforcement structure; downstream synthesis of enforcement and gatekeeping effects

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Selective termination based on disability diagnosis reveals personhood boundary's interaction with disability status
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Identified in absence inventory but requires disability studies expertise beyond current scope; omega material for specialized analysis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Islamic jurisprudence (ensoulment at 120 days), Buddhist gradual-consciousness models offer alternative boundary determinations
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Identified in absence inventory but requires comparative religious law expertise; cross-cultural analysis deferred to specialized treatment

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Neurological capacity for pain experience as alternative personhood marker
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Subsumed by gradualist reading's developmental milestone framework; distinct observable but not structurally independent

omegas.description: Viability threshold shifts with medical technology (artificial wombs, extreme prematurity survival). Does advancing technology collapse viability reading into conception reading by making all embryos 'viable'? Boundary stability depends on technological stasis assumption.
omegas.source: Viability reading analysis + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Selective termination for disability diagnosis reveals personhood boundary's interaction with disability status. Does fetus with Down syndrome have different moral status than neurotypical fetus? Disability rights frameworks contest this but are absent from mainstream abortion discourse.
omegas.source: Deferred axis disability_rights_dimension + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Non-Western personhood frameworks (Islamic 120-day ensoulment, Buddhist gradual-consciousness) offer alternative boundary determinations. Are these structurally distinct readings or cultural variations on gradualism? Requires comparative religious law expertise.
omegas.source: Deferred axis non_western_frameworks + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: All four kernel readings are adjudicated by institutions historically controlled by men. Does the personhood boundary debate obscure a prior question: who has authority to define personhood for pregnant persons? Beneficiary scan suggests male-dominated religious and legal institutions benefit from framing as metaphysical rather than power question.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + extraction tension analysis

omegas.description: Is the personhood boundary a stable kernel or does it drift under pressure? Exception regimes (rape, incest, health) reveal boundary instability: if fetus has full personhood at conception, why do exceptions exist? Suggests conception reading may be tangled_rope masquerading as mountain.
omegas.source: Mechanism analysis (exception regimes) + F03 (Hasty Generalization) check

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Multi-lens scan applied legal philosophy, bioethics, feminist theory, and political economy lenses. Dark matter probes surfaced disability rights and non-Western frameworks (deferred for expertise reasons). Kernel decomposition into four readings passes pairwise independence test: each reading has distinct victim-set entry point and enforcement structure. Three additional axes (enforcement extractiveness, medical gatekeeping, class stratification) measure independent structural dimensions orthogonal to boundary location.
